title: Add a User Flow
bottom_line: Describe one new flow. Claude checks it is not already listed, confirms it exists in the code, and adds it to user-flows.md.

sections.heading: Type the command followed by a description of the flow

blocks.code: /user-flows:add-user-flow <free-text description of the new user flow>
blocks.caption: The description is free text.

blocks.title: Example
blocks.code: /user-flows:add-user-flow let users export their order history as CSV

blocks.title: Which command to use
rows: You want to add one specific flow, journey or scenario, such as a single flow the client asked for.
You want many flows re-derived from the whole session's code changes.
You want the list regenerated or extracted from the codebase at large.

blocks.title: Before you start
items: Nothing beyond Claude Code is needed. The skill reads the code and writes `user-flows.md` at the project root.
The plugin has no environment variables and no plugin settings.
You do not need a `user-flows.md` yet. If there is none, one is created.

sections.heading: It first checks whether the flow is already listed

blocks.title: What happens to your description

nodes.label: Look for it in the code
Stop: says the feature is missing

blocks.caption: When a matching flow is found, user-flows.md is not changed.

before.label: Your words
before.text: "Allow buyers to back out of an order before it ships."

blocks.caption: These count as the same flow even with no words in common, so nothing is added.

blocks.text: The check judges what the flow does, not how it is worded. Two flows with the same steps and the same outcome, differing only in data values, count as the same flow. This is the same rule `/user-flows:extract-user-flows` uses.
When a match is found, it reports the existing flow's ID, its name and why it matches, and makes no changes to the file.

sections.heading: A new flow is grounded in your code, never invented

nodes.label: Entry point
nodes.note: Where the flow starts in the app.

nodes.label: Elements involved
nodes.note: The interactive elements the person uses.

nodes.label: What they do
nodes.note: What those elements actually do in the code.

blocks.title: What Claude traces in the code

blocks.text: This makes the flow based on evidence, not on your description alone. If your description does not match anything in the code, Claude says so and stops, instead of writing a flow for a feature that does not exist.

sections.heading: The new flow gets the next ID and nothing else moves

cards.title: Same shape as others
cards.text: Written in the exact format extraction uses (Actor, Precondition, Steps, Expected and Source), with the same rule against duplicates, so the file stays consistent.

cards.title: Next free ID
cards.text: It gets the next ID after the highest one in the whole file. An ID is never reused.

cards.title: Under its area heading
cards.text: Placed under the matching area heading. If the area is new, the heading is created.

cards.title: Other flows untouched
cards.text: Every other flow stays exactly as it was: no reformatting, reordering or rewording.

cards.title: Header date updated
cards.text: The `generated:` date in the header is updated. Granularity and area stay as they were, or as set at creation for a new file.

sections.heading: If there is no user-flows.md yet, it starts one

after.label: New file
after.text: A `user-flows.md` with the standard header and no flows yet, then your one flow is added to it.

blocks.title: Header of a newly created file

blocks.text: It does not run a full extraction first. Only the one flow you described is added.

sections.heading: If you already have user-flow tests, a test is added too

nodes.label: New flow written to the file
test-user-flow runs and adds a test
Skipped, with a pointer to test-user-flow

blocks.caption: Existing user-flow tests are found by looking for a folder with `# user-flow:` marker comments.

blocks.text: When there are no user-flow tests yet, Claude mentions that `/user-flows:test-user-flow` can set them up.

sections.heading: The report tells you which of two things happened

cards.title: Already listed
cards.text: The ID and name of the existing flow that blocked the add. No changes were made.

cards.title: Flow added
cards.text: The new flow's ID, name and area, plus the outcome of the test sync.

blocks.caption: It does not paste the whole file back into the conversation.

next_action.text: Run `/user-flows:add-user-flow` followed by a description of the flow you want added.
next_action.detail: For example: `/user-flows:add-user-flow let users export their order history as CSV`.
